meta.title: LazyDocs — Documentation at your own pace
meta.description: Write Markdown, get a fast, searchable and themeable documentation site. Open source, built with React and Vite, with dark mode and five languages built in.

hero.title: Documentation,
hero.subtitle: Drop Markdown files in a folder and LazyDocs turns them into a fast, searchable docs site, with themes, dark mode and five languages. No framework to learn, no backend to run.
hero.note: Free and MIT licensed. Clone it and it's yours.

mock.aria: Preview of a documentation page built with LazyDocs
mock.title: Quick start
mock.description: Create your first documentation page in three minutes.
mock.heading: Your first page
mock.paragraphEnd: and the sidebar picks it up on its own.
mock.paragraph2: Save the file and the page is live. Its title, description and keywords come straight from the frontmatter.

how.title: From folder to website
how.lead: No CLI to learn and no config file to master. If you can write a README, you can ship your docs today.

steps.title: Clone it
steps.text: Grab the repository and install. The dev server starts on port 3000 with hot reload.

steps.title: Write Markdown
steps.text: Add .md files under public/docs/. Folders become sections and frontmatter becomes metadata.

steps.title: Deploy anywhere
steps.text: One build gives you a static site with its sitemap. Vercel, Netlify or GitHub Pages all work.

writing.title: Write Markdown.
writing.lead: Everything you already know works: GitHub-flavored tables, task lists, images and fenced code. LazyDocs takes care of the typography, the anchors and the highlighting.

points.title: Frontmatter, not config
points.text: Title, description, keywords and order live at the top of each file, and feed the sidebar, the search and the meta tags.

points.title: Code blocks that read well
points.text: Syntax highlighting with line numbers and a copy button, tuned for every theme in light and dark.

points.title: An anchor for every heading
points.text: Each heading gets its own link and a place in the table of contents, so any section is one click away.

sample.title: Deploying
sample.description: Ship your docs in two commands.
sample.intro: Build the site, then upload the dist folder.

navigation.title: Folders in.
navigation.lead: The sidebar is generated from your folder structure every time you run dev or build. Move a file and the navigation follows.

points.title: Order on your terms
points.text: List folders in _sidebar-order.json and set order in each page's frontmatter. The rest falls into place alphabetically.

points.title: Readers never get lost
points.text: Breadcrumbs, previous and next links, a table of contents and a reading progress bar on every page.

points.title: Nothing to keep in sync
points.text: sidebar.json is rebuilt on every run, so it can never drift from the files you actually have.

themes.title: Four themes.
themes.lead: Pick one with a single line in config.json. Every theme ships light and dark variants with its own syntax colors, and readers switch between them with a smooth fade.
themes.custom: Want your own? A theme is a single CSS file of color tokens. Copy one from src/themes/ and change the values.

search.title: Search that forgives typos
search.text: Full-text fuzzy search opens with ⌘K. Titles weigh more than body text, and the index is cached so results show up as you type.

i18n.title: Five languages, one click
i18n.text: The interface speaks English, Spanish, French, German and Portuguese, and follows the reader's browser. Try it here.

seo.title: Ready for search engines
seo.text: Meta tags from frontmatter, Open Graph and Twitter cards, JSON-LD and a sitemap generated on every build.
seo.resultText: Create your first documentation page in three minutes. Write Markdown, save, done.

dark.title: Dark mode that remembers
dark.text: Follows the system preference, remembers each reader's choice and fades between modes instead of flashing.

code.title: Copy, paste, move on
code.text: Every code block has line numbers and a one-click copy button, so readers never select by hand.

faq.title: Questions,
faq.lead: The short version. The documentation has the long one.

items.q: Do I need to know React?
items.a: No. You write Markdown and edit one JSON file. React only matters if you want custom components or a different layout.
In public/docs/. Each folder becomes a sidebar section and each .md file a page, served at /docs/folder/file.

items.q: How do I change the name, logo or colors?
items.a: Everything lives in public/config.json: the site name, logos for light and dark mode, navbar and footer links, and the color theme.
Anywhere that serves static files and falls back to index.html. The repository already includes a vercel.json, and the README has a one-click Deploy to Vercel button.

items.q: Can I make my own theme?
items.a: Yes. Copy one of the files in src/themes/, change the color tokens and set its file name as colorTheme in config.json.
Yes. LazyDocs is open source under the MIT license: use it, fork it, and ship it in commercial projects.

cta.title: Go on, be lazy.
cta.subtitle: Clone the repository, write your first page and have it online before your coffee gets cold.

footer.tagline: Markdown in, documentation out. A lightweight docs platform built with React and Vite.
